To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the degree of SFP capitalization into land rental prices depends on the scarcity of entitlements and the implementation model.

(a) the degree of SFP capitalization into land rental prices is positively related to the degree of land supply elasticity, (b) the degree of land rent capitalization is negatively related to the degree to which land rental prices are determined by the land supply elasticity, and (c) the degree of capitalisation is negatively related to land rental prices.
the Fischler CAP-reform has had an impact on rental prices and the degree of capitalisation of single farm payments into land values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a graphical and empirical analysis of the impacts of the CAP reform of 2003 on the rental prices of agricultural land and the capitalization effects of single farm payments.
the question of whether the decoupling of SFP will lead to a decline in land rental prices in the long run.
the question of what happens with land rents when the Common Agricultural Policy is reformed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fischler CAP Reform has not reduced the degree of capitalisation of direct payments into land prices.
the Fischler reform has not led to a decline in the degree of SFP capitalization into land rental prices.
the Fischler CAP Reform has had a positive effect on the land market in Germany.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Fischler reform has led to an increase of the degree of capitalizaiton, which is in line with the expectations of policy makers.
decoupled payments are capitalized to a higher degree than coupled payments, but that the degree of this capitalization depends on the supply elasticity of the land market.
the degree of SFP capitalization into land rental prices is mainly determined by the supply and demand for SFP entitlements and the supply elasticity of land.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree of decoupling of SFP is a crucial determinant of the degree of capitalisation of SFP into land prices.
the degree of the capitalization of SFP depends on the supply elasticity of land, the implementation model and the relative scarcity/surplus in SFP entitlements.
decoupling of SFP is a double-edged sword.
